# Foundation Requirements Quality Checklist: Configure Vite React TypeScript foundation

**Purpose**: Review the issue-driven requirements quality for the repository foundation, including issue traceability, responsiveness, accessibility, and branch workflow expectations.
**Created**: 2026-09-19
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 - Are the project foundation requirements explicitly covered for local setup, build validation, and lint validation in the current spec? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-002, §FR-003]
- [x] CHK002 - Are the repository readiness requirements for future feature branches clearly documented as a separate requirement from the app runtime baseline? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK003 - Are the business-context requirements for Bramhecha Ceramics and the static hosting model clearly reflected in the scope without inventing additional product claims? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, §FR-006]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK004 - Is the phrase "working local development baseline" defined with measurable criteria for setup, launch, and contributor readiness? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001]
- [x] CHK005 - Is "validates the app can compile successfully from a clean setup" sufficiently specific to support objective verification? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK006 - Is the requirement for "future feature branches" clear enough to distinguish branch workflow expectations from actual implementation steps? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK007 - Do the foundation requirements remain consistent with the repository governance rules for issue-driven work, branch isolation, and PR-based delivery? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, Constitution §4, §5]
- [x] CHK008 - Are the accessibility and responsive development expectations consistent with the project’s stated static front-end and GitHub Pages target? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, Constitution §1, §2]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK009 - Do the acceptance criteria in the issue and the spec align without adding new business or technical requirements beyond the original request? [Acceptance Criteria, Issue #2, Spec §User Story 1-3]
- [x] CHK010 - Are the success criteria measurable enough to tell whether the foundation is ready for ongoing feature development without relying on vague wording? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §SC-002, §SC-003, §SC-004]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK011 - Are requirements defined for the primary setup scenario, the validation failure scenario, and the recovery path when the project environment is incomplete? [Coverage, Edge Case]
- [x] CHK012 - Are the branch readiness and future feature sequencing scenarios documented clearly enough to support planning without implicitly prescribing implementation details? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 3]

## Accessibility and UX Quality

- [x] CHK013 - Are keyboard access and focus-state expectations for future interactive UI defined in a way that can be carried into later feature requirements? [Accessibility, Gap]
- [x] CHK014 - Are responsive behavior expectations for mobile and larger screens clearly scoped as design requirements rather than implementation-specific UI choices? [Responsive UX, Gap]
- [x] CHK015 - Does the requirement set avoid inventing product claims or brand statements that are not supported by the verified project source material? [Content Integrity, Spec §FR-005]

## GitHub Traceability and Workflow

- [x] CHK016 - Is the source issue traceability clear enough to connect the foundation requirements to GitHub Issue #2 and its acceptance criteria? [Traceability, Issue #2, Spec §Issue Traceability]
- [x] CHK017 - Are the branch and PR expectations clearly framed as process constraints rather than implementation details, without contradicting the main-branch protection policy? [Workflow, Constitution §4, §5]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
